title: Compile, capture, and register
brief: Fuse a chain of six pointwise ops by hand in Triton and with torch.compile, replay a launch-bound decode-like loop from a CUDA graph, and register a Triton kernel as a custom op that torch.compile traces with fullgraph=True.
hints: The first call to a Triton kernel and the first call to a torch.compile'd function each compile for several seconds. The tests warm up before they time, but your own experiments should too.
Mask every load and store in the Triton kernel with offs < n. The tests use sizes such as 1, 7, and 4097 that are not multiples of the block size.

To read what Inductor wrote, call torch._inductor.utils.run_and_get_code(compiled_fn, x). It returns the result and a list of source strings. Turn off the FX graph cache with torch._inductor.config.patch so a cached graph doesn't hide the code.
CUDA graph capture needs a warmup on a side stream, static input and output tensors, and no host synchronization inside the capture. Copy new data into the static input, then call graph.replay().

A custom_op that wraps a Triton kernel needs a register_fake so torch.compile can trace it. A triton_op doesn't: launch the kernel with wrap_triton(kernel)[grid](...) and the compiler traces through it.
Both custom ops need mutates_args. This kernel writes only a fresh output tensor, so the right value is an empty tuple.
